title: Article 21 — Protection of life and personal liberty

content.overview: Article 21 provides that no person shall be deprived of life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law. After Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India, that procedure must be fair, just and reasonable. Life includes more than animal existence; personal liberty is a wide residual freedom subject to lawful and fair procedure.

sections.heading: Text
sections.body: No person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law. Verify official wording.

sections.heading: Historical position
sections.body: HISTORICAL: A.K. Gopalan associated a narrow, compartmentalised reading of Article 21. CURRENT: Maneka Gandhi requires fair, just and reasonable procedure and integration with Articles 14 and 19 where engaged (golden triangle).

sections.heading: Scope (practice-oriented)
sections.body: Article 21 has been applied to a wide range of interests connected with life and liberty in decided cases. Do not invent new rights without authority. Always identify the statute or executive action and the procedure used.

sections.heading: Track B
sections.body: Plead the deprivation, the source of power, the procedure followed, and why it fails fairness or legality. BSA and criminal procedure rules govern fact-finding; they do not replace the constitutional standard.
